scope: Proposition 8.5 (Compatible dual relations) of the manuscript “A Counterexample to Kurosh’s Division-Ring Problem” (preprints/A-Counterexample-to-Kuroshs-Division-Ring-Problem-September-23-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 201 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 9195b0a83fc63370), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 27. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: For any finite nonempty collection of independent generic size-b points Pi, there is a g-dimensional space G{Pi} ⊆ ⨁︂ i H∗ Pi with the following properties. 1. Projection to each H∗ Pi is an isomorphism. 2. It annihilates all joint paired responses, with both arrows arbitrary. 3. For a fixed generic arrow between Pi, Pj, the annihilator in H∗ Pi ⊕ H∗ Pj of the variable reverse-arrow image is exactly the restriction of G{Pi}. 4. On adjoining independent blocks, restriction of the larger space is the original space after scalar extension. For one block this space is H∗ P . These statements include g = 0.
